item.title: “It was not committed at a place within public view”: Rajasthan High Court sets aside 1994’s conviction for caste abuse
item.description: “The incident is averred to have transpired within close precincts, specifically within the four corners of the walls of the shop premises. This description denotes a spatially confined and enclosed environment, shielded from casual public access and observation.” The post “It was not committed at a place within public view”: Rajasthan High Court sets aside 1994’s conviction for caste abuse appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: The Consolidation of Labour Laws in India: Promise or Precarity?
item.description: The real test of the of India's Labour Codes lies not only in enforcement but also in the structural limitations of the Codes themselves. Political will, Centre-State coordination, and genuine consultations with workers are essential to bridge the gap between legislative ambition and ground reality. by Kartik Kanodia* The post The Consolidation of Labour Laws in India: Promise or Precarity? appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Madras High Court: Law and order no ground for disobedience of judicial orders; Officials held accountable for ignoring directions in Thiruparankundram hill lamp case
item.description: “Law and order cannot be a ground for flouting a court’s order, as that would be inexcusable, amount to a breakdown of law and order, and ultimately lead to paralysis of the constitutional machinery.” The post Madras High Court: Law and order no ground for disobedience of judicial orders; Officials held accountable for ignoring directions in Thiruparankundram hill lamp case appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Trade Mark registration or Online Listing alone doesn’t confer Territorial Jurisdiction in infringement suit: Delhi High Court
item.description: The Court held that “the conclusion arrived at by the learned Single Judge that this Court did not have the territorial jurisdiction to entertain the suit cannot be faulted.” The post Trade Mark registration or Online Listing alone doesn’t confer Territorial Jurisdiction in infringement suit: Delhi High Court appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Advises IFC on Nephrocare Health Services Limited IPO
item.description: The IPO comprised a fresh issue and an offer for sale, with IFC divesting part of its shareholding. Nephrocare’s equity shares were listed on Indian stock exchanges on 17 December 2025. The post Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Advises IFC on Nephrocare Health Services Limited IPO appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends transfer of Justice Soumen Sen as Chief Justice of Kerala High Court
item.description: Justice Soumen Sen was appointed as Chief Justice of the High Court of Meghalaya on 26-09-2025 and took oath on 08-10-2025. The post Supreme Court Collegium recommends transfer of Justice Soumen Sen as Chief Justice of Kerala High Court appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: SPREE Circular is for awareness only; Compliance to take place once Social Security Code Rules Are Notified: ESIC Clarifies
item.description: ESIC issued a circular clarifying the intent of circular on 11-12-2025 and compliance under Social Security Code. The post SPREE Circular is for awareness only; Compliance to take place once Social Security Code Rules Are Notified: ESIC Clarifies appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Kerala High Court denies Bail to Ex-Devaswom Board Officials in Sabarimala Gold Misappropriation Case
item.description: The incidents that led to the case has deeply hurt the religious sentiments of scores of Ayyappa devotees and pilgrims. The post Kerala High Court denies Bail to Ex-Devaswom Board Officials in Sabarimala Gold Misappropriation Case appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: “Gustakh-e-nabi ki ek saja, sar tan se juda” is challenge to sovereignty and integrity of India: Allahabad High Court
item.description: The slogan was first used in Pakistan and thereafter was spread to India and has been widely misused by certain Muslims just to intimidate people of other religions and to challenge the authority of the State. The post “Gustakh-e-nabi ki ek saja, sar tan se juda” is challenge to sovereignty and integrity of India: Allahabad High Court appeared first on SCC Times.
